sources.claimScope: Completion of the present temple around 1809 under the patronage of the Sabarna Roy Chowdhury family and an earlier structure commissioned by King Manasingha in the early 16th century; the sandstone image of Kali with three eyes, four hands and a gold tongue, attributed to Atmaram Giri and Brahmananda Giri; status as one of the 51 Shakti Peethas and the tradition that Sati's right toe fell here; the Natmandir of 1835, the Jor Bangla, the Harkath Tala, the Sosthi Tala altar to Sosti, Shitala and Mangal Chandi, the Kundupukur tank and the Nakuleshwar Mahadev temple; opening hours 05:00-14:00 and 17:00-22:30; Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose airport and Howrah and Sealdah as nearest stations.

identity.spiritualSignificanceShort: Kalighat is counted among the fifty-one Shakti Peethas, the tradition holding that the toes of Sati's right foot fell at this spot. The goddess is worshipped here as Kali in a sandstone image with three eyes, four hands and a protruding gold tongue, attributed to the saints Atmaram Giri and Brahmananda Giri. It is one of the busiest pilgrimage centres in eastern India, drawing hundreds of thousands of devotees a year, above all at Kali Puja and Durga Puja.

narrative.documentedHistory:
The site's temple history is traced back several centuries, an earlier structure being attributed to the patronage of King Manasingha in the early sixteenth century.

The building standing today is of the turn of the nineteenth century. Santosh Roy Chowdhury began its construction in 1798 and the work, carried out under the patronage of the Sabarna Roy Chowdhury family, took eleven years and was completed around 1809. The Natmandir, the large rectangular veranda from which the sanctum can be seen, was added in 1835.

In 2024 the temple underwent its first major modern renovation, funded jointly by the Kolkata Municipal Corporation and the Reliance Foundation. Existing terracotta detail was preserved while damaged elements were restored and gold was added to the spires.
narrative.architectureStyle: Ath-chala (eight-roofed) Bengal temple architecture, with gabled roofs carrying terracotta motifs of deities and natural forms, and a truncated eight-faced dome with three spires
narrative.sacredTank: Kundupukur, the sacred tank to the south-east of the main temple
